issues.detail: The skill covers mostly the happy path and gives no guidance on error scenarios or edge cases such as invalid or missing API keys, source rate-limit or timeout failures, wildcard DNS, empty results, or deduplicating results across multiple domains.

scenarios.name: source-attribution-and-key-config
scenarios.rationale: Both show -cs and -oJ and put shodan and virustotal as YAML lists in ~/.config/subfinder/provider-config.yaml, but neither says subfinder works without keys and returns more with them as plainly as the rubric asks; A does say keys give 'significantly more results' and lists the free sources, while B gives a more thorough per-source counting workflow and handles both the sources and source JSON fields.

scenarios.name: live-check-pipeline-with-rate-limit
scenarios.rationale: B provides the correct subfinder-to-httpx pipeline with -silent, -status-code, -title, and rate-limit throttling plus scope caveats, fully satisfying the rubric, while A refuses entirely and gives no technical content.

scenarios.name: recursive-flag-and-active-gaps
scenarios.rationale: B correctly explains that -recursive only restricts to recursive-capable sources with no depth-limiting flag (plus a workaround for depth filtering) and clearly flags active techniques (puredns/shuffledns, zone transfer) as requiring authorization, matching the rubric closely, while A never mentions -recursive or its actual semantics and never explicitly states there's no depth limit, though it does cover active techniques and authorization reminders.
